primary_attribution_followup.finding: Cubic real-zero finiteness has a direct classical antecedent. Nonintegral cases retain unresolved priority. No formal theorem changed.

human_reorganization: Section 9 proves product integrability before Fubini for the actual real/imaginary Gaussian shifts of the quadratic arithmetic flow, preserving variance 2s and opposite time signs t-s versus t+s. No quadratic zero reality is inferred.

The polynomial counterexample is indexed by m>=1, corresponding to formal normalized index n=m-1. Complete Gaussian integration-by-parts and finite differential-heat calculations recover values two despite normalized even-real polynomial compact convergence to one. No split-real-root hypothesis is asserted for those polynomials.

The compact-tail mass escape and common subcritical imaginary-axis Gaussian-growth sufficient condition tau<1/4 are explicitly labelled fully proved human classical deductions, not additional formal theorems or necessary growth classifications.

The new material is classical Gaussian integral/topology reasoning and gives no priority claim, A(2) threshold relation or RH implication. Pólya 1923 full-text comparison remains pending; the already inspected Pólya 1927 cubic antecedent and Cardon multiplier-premise distinctions remain authoritative.

Section 8 reconstructs the actual coefficient-aware fourth-derivative cancellation uniformly for 1<a<=5/4. The normalized endpoint weight b*u^(b-1) has unit integral; no common raw pointwise integrable majorant is assumed. A common derivative integral bound, one further integration by parts and a principal-power reciprocal-frequency estimate yield the actual x^(-1/2) uniform absolute Fourier rate.

The displayed complete Bell polynomial, the elementary global superexponential tail majorant and explicit sqrt(2)/2 reciprocal-profile derivative bound are human reconstructions/refinements of the verified mechanism, not new named formal theorems with optimized constants. The cutoff coefficient/profile extension to b=0 is explicitly distinct from evaluating the original cutoff integral there.

For each fixed nonzero time, the retained linear leading-coefficient lower bound gives relative error C/((a-1)*sqrt(x)), relative diagonal convergence in its parameter-dependent region and the exact real-zero radius max(1,(K/(a-1))^2). Constants are not numerically identified; no sharp scale, complex-zero escape rate, uniformity in time, A(2) relation or RH conclusion follows.

The full rectangle cannot have any bounded relative error near order one: at each chosen arbitrarily large nonzero quadratic coordinate, continuity leaves a nonzero scaled limit while the leading coefficient vanishes. This is compatible with the parameter-dependent positive theorem. Classical endpoint/integration-by-parts methods are credited, and arithmetic priority remains unresolved.
